title: Optics
summary: Shadows, reflection, mirrors, refraction, lenses, colors, and the eye.
cards.0.h: Light travels in straight lines: shadows
cards.0.p: Light travels along straight lines. That is why a shadow forms behind an opaque obstacle. A point source makes a full shadow (umbra). An extended source also makes a partial shadow (penumbra) around it.
cards.0.key: No light from any point of the source reaches the umbra, and light from part of the source reaches the penumbra. This is how eclipses happen.
cards.1.p: As light moves away from the source it spreads over a larger area, and the illuminance decreases: E = I·cosθ/d². When the distance doubles, the illuminance drops to one quarter.
cards.1.key: I is the luminous intensity, and its unit is the candela. θ is the angle between the ray and the normal. The unit of luminous flux is the lumen, and the unit of illuminance is the lux (lumen/m²).
cards.1.once.soru: If you move a desk lamp twice as far from a book, how well is the book lit?
cards.1.once.secenekler.0.neden: The same light spreads over 4 times the area. So illuminance decreases with the square of the distance.
cards.1.once.secenekler.1.neden: The distance doubles, but the area the light spreads over grows 4 times.
cards.1.once.secenekler.2.neden: Light spreads over a larger area as it moves away.
cards.2.p: In reflection, the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection. The angles are measured from the normal, the line perpendicular to the surface. A smooth surface gives specular reflection, and a rough surface gives diffuse reflection.
cards.2.key: The incident ray, the normal, and the reflected ray lie in the same plane. In diffuse reflection, too, every ray obeys this rule.
cards.3.p: The image in a plane mirror is virtual, upright, and the same size as the object. The image forms behind the mirror, at the same distance as the object. If the mirror is rotated by α, the reflected ray rotates by 2α.
cards.3.key: A mirror actually reverses front and back, not left and right. The field of view is the region between the lines drawn from the image of the eye to the edges of the mirror.
cards.4.h: Concave mirror: focus and special rays
cards.4.p: In a spherical mirror, the center of curvature is shown with C and the focus with F, and f = r/2. A concave mirror converges light. The image forms where two special reflected rays cross.
cards.4.svg#4: ① parallel to the axis → passes through F
cards.4.svg#5: ② through F → returns parallel to the axis
cards.4.svg#6: ③ through C → returns along itself
cards.4.key: If the reflected rays cross, the image is real. If only their extensions cross, it is virtual.
cards.4.etk.soru: Explore the key points of a concave mirror.
cards.4.etk.noktalar.0.acik: This is the axis of symmetry that passes through the vertex of the mirror and the center of curvature.
cards.4.etk.noktalar.1.acik: This is the center of the sphere the mirror is part of. A ray coming through C returns along itself.
cards.4.etk.noktalar.2.acik: Rays coming parallel to the axis pass through here after reflecting. f = r / 2.
cards.4.etk.noktalar.3.acik: This is the point where the mirror meets the principal axis. f and r are measured from here.
cards.4.etk.noktalar.4.acik: In a concave mirror the reflecting face is on the inside. That is why the mirror converges light.
cards.4.once.soru: You can gather sunlight at one point with a concave mirror and burn paper. What is that point called?
cards.4.once.secenekler.0.neden: Rays coming in parallel gather at the focus after reflecting.
cards.4.once.secenekler.1.neden: The center of curvature is twice as far as the focus. The rays do not gather there.
cards.4.once.secenekler.2.neden: The vertex is a point on the mirror. The rays gather in front of the mirror.
cards.5.p: In a concave mirror, if the object is outside F the image is real and inverted. If the object is between F and the mirror, the image is virtual, upright, and enlarged. A convex mirror always gives a virtual, upright, and reduced image.
cards.5.key: If the object is at F, no image forms. A convex mirror gives a wide field of view, so it is used as a rearview mirror. The focal length of a convex mirror is taken as negative.
cards.6.p: When light passes into another medium at an angle, it bends because its speed changes. The refractive index is n = c/v, and it is 1.33 for water. According to Snell's law, n₁·sinθ₁ = n₂·sinθ₂. In the medium with the larger index, the ray bends toward the normal.
cards.6.key: Optical density is not mass density. For example, oil is lighter than water, but its refractive index is larger.
cards.7.h: Total internal reflection and the critical angle
cards.7.p: Light passing from a medium with a larger index into one with a smaller index bends away from the normal. When the angle of incidence exceeds the critical angle, the light cannot get out and is reflected back completely. This is called total internal reflection.
cards.7.key: The critical angle is found with sin θc = n₂/n₁. In a fiber cable, light travels by total internal reflection in the glass core. The sparkle of a diamond comes from this too.
cards.8.p: Light from an object in water bends away from the normal as it comes out into air. Since the eye extends the rays straight back, it sees the object higher than it is. That is why a pool looks shallower than it is.
cards.8.key: A pool 2 m deep looks about 1.5 m deep when you look straight down. A fish in the water sees a bird in the air higher than it is.
cards.8.once.soru: You look from above at a coin on the bottom of a pool. Where does the coin appear?
cards.8.once.secenekler.0.neden: Light bends as it leaves the water. The eye extends it straight back and sees the coin higher up.
cards.8.once.secenekler.1.neden: Since light bends at the water surface, the coin appears displaced.
cards.8.once.secenekler.2.neden: Refraction makes the coin look raised.
cards.9.p: A lens with thin edges converges light and is called a converging lens. A lens with thick edges spreads light and is called a diverging lens. A ray coming parallel to the axis passes through the focus. A ray through the center is not deviated.
cards.9.key: A converging lens resembles a concave mirror, and a diverging lens a convex mirror. If the object is between F and a converging lens, the image is virtual and enlarged. This is how a magnifying glass works.
cards.9.once.soru: You can gather sunlight at one point with a magnifying glass. What are the edges of a magnifying glass like?
cards.9.once.secenekler.0.neden: A lens that is thick in the middle and thin at the edges converges light.
cards.9.once.secenekler.1.neden: A lens with thick edges spreads light.
cards.9.once.secenekler.2.neden: Flat glass does not converge light.
cards.10.p: For mirrors and lenses, 1/f = 1/do + 1/di. The magnification is found with m = −di/do. If m is negative the image is inverted, and if it is positive the image is upright.
cards.10.key: d<sub>o</sub> is the distance of the object, and d<sub>i</sub> is the distance of the image. For a virtual image, di is taken as negative. If |m| > 1, the image is enlarged.
cards.10.etk.soru: A concave mirror or converging lens (f > 0). Move the object closer and farther. Where is the image?
cards.10.etk.yorum.0.1: The image is virtual, upright, and enlarged. The object is between F and the mirror (lens).
cards.10.etk.yorum.1.1: The image is real and inverted. The object is outside F.
cards.10.once.soru: 1/f = 1/do + 1/di. For a concave mirror, f = 10 cm and the object is 15 cm away. How many cm away is the image?
cards.10.once.secenekler.1.neden: Distances are not added. You take the difference of their reciprocals: 1/10 − 1/15.
cards.11.h: Calculations for convex mirrors and diverging lenses
cards.11.p: For a convex mirror and a diverging lens, f is negative. If f = −10 cm and the object is 15 cm away, then d<sub>i</sub> = −6 cm. This image is virtual, upright, and reduced.
cards.11.key: 1/di = −1/10 − 1/15 = −1/6 and m = 0.4. Wherever the object is, these two give a virtual, upright, and reduced image.
cards.11.once.soru: A car's side mirror says "Objects in mirror are closer than they appear". Why?
cards.11.once.secenekler.0.neden: A convex mirror gives a virtual and reduced image. So a vehicle looks farther away than it is.
cards.11.once.secenekler.1.neden: The warning is because of the shape of the mirror.
cards.11.once.secenekler.2.neden: If it enlarged them, objects would look closer.
cards.12.p: The refractive index of glass changes with color. That is why white light splits into its colors in a prism. Red bends the least, and violet the most. A rainbow forms by refraction and reflection in raindrops.
cards.12.key: In glass, violet light travels more slowly than red. That is why the refractive index for violet is larger.
cards.12.once.soru: Where must the Sun be for you to see a rainbow?
cards.12.once.secenekler.0.neden: Light refracts and reflects in the drops in front of you and comes back to you.
cards.12.once.secenekler.1.neden: When you face the Sun, the light reflected from the drops does not reach you.
cards.12.once.secenekler.2.neden: When the Sun is very high, the rainbow stays below the horizon.
cards.13.h: Colors in light and in paint
cards.13.p: The primary colors of light are red, green, and blue. When the three combine, white light forms. An object appears in the color it reflects from the light that falls on it. A filter lets only its own color through.
cards.13.svg#8: Paint absorbs some colors and reflects the rest.
cards.13.key: In paint the primary colors are cyan, magenta, and yellow. A red apple looks black in blue light.
cards.14.p: The eye is like a converging lens, and a real, inverted, and reduced image forms on the retina. A nearsighted person cannot see far objects clearly and uses a diverging lens. A farsighted person cannot see near objects clearly and uses a converging lens.
cards.14.key: In a nearsighted eye the image falls in front of the retina, and in a farsighted eye behind it. A nearsighted eye gets a lens with thick edges, and a farsighted eye a lens with thin edges.
cards.15.p:
• In reflection, the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.
• A plane mirror gives a virtual, upright image of the same size.
• n₁·sinθ₁ = n₂·sinθ₂.
• Beyond the critical angle there is total internal reflection.
• For mirrors and lenses, 1/f = 1/do + 1/di.
• Nearsighted eyes get a diverging lens, farsighted eyes a converging lens.
cards.15.svg#11: small n → large n: bends toward the normal
quiz.0.q: An object is placed 30 cm in front of a converging lens with a focal length of 20 cm. How many cm from the lens does the image form?
quiz.0.e: 1/d<sub>i</sub> = 1/20 − 1/30 = 1/60, so d<sub>i</sub> = +60 cm. Since this value is positive, the image is real and inverted. The magnification is m = −60/30 = −2.
quiz.1.q: Is the image in each case real or virtual? Put it in the right group.
quiz.1.e: In a concave mirror, if the object is outside F the image is real and inverted. The image on the retina is real too. A plane mirror, a convex mirror, and a diverging lens give virtual images. In a concave mirror, the image of an object between F and the mirror is also virtual.
quiz.2.q: Match each case with the related optical principle or device.
quiz.2.e: In a nearsighted eye the image falls in front of the retina, and a diverging lens is used. In a farsighted eye the image falls behind the retina, and a converging lens is used. A convex mirror gives a wide field of view. Fiber optics relies on total internal reflection. A pool looks shallow because light bends as it passes from water into air.
quiz.3.q: Light traveling inside glass with a refractive index of 1.5 toward air strikes the glass-air surface at an angle of incidence of 45°. What happens? (sin 45° ≈ 0.71)
quiz.3.o.0: It passes into air, bending toward the normal
quiz.3.o.1: It passes into air without bending or changing direction
quiz.3.o.2: The angle of refraction is 90°, and it skims the surface
quiz.3.o.3: It cannot pass into air and is totally reflected
quiz.3.e: For the critical angle, sin θc = 1/1.5 ≈ 0.67, so θc ≈ 42°. Since the angle of incidence, 45°, is larger than this, the light undergoes total internal reflection.
quiz.3.y.0: Light passing from a larger index to a smaller index bends away from the normal. What is more, the critical angle is exceeded here.
quiz.3.y.1: Light keeps its direction only if it arrives along the normal. Light arriving at 45° is either refracted or reflected.
quiz.3.y.2: The angle of refraction is 90° only when the angle of incidence equals the critical angle. sin 45° ≈ 0.71 is larger than 0.67. So 45° is larger than θc ≈ 42°.
A:ozet: Enlarge a shadow, bounce a laser onto a target, count images in angled mirrors, find the image in a concave mirror, bend light, catch total internal reflection, and work out color in light and the nearsighted eye.
A:adimlar.0.metin: Since light travels along straight lines, a shadow forms behind the ball. The diameter of the ball is 10 cm, and the screen is 120 cm from the lamp. Place the ball so that the diameter of the shadow is exactly 3 times that of the ball. Then try the extended source too.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.tamam: With the point source, the distance from the lamp to the ball is 40 cm and to the screen 120 cm. Since the distance is three times as large, the shadow is three times as large too, that is 30 cm. Similar triangles show this.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.ipucu: The shadow grows by the ratio of the lamp-to-screen distance to the lamp-to-ball distance: 120 / d = 3.
A:adimlar.1.metin: In reflection, the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection. Change the angle of the laser and send the reflected ray to the target.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.tamam: The ray that arrived at 40° reflected at 40° on the other side of the normal and hit the target.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.ipucu: The target is at the same height as the laser. The ray goes to the mirror and comes back at the same angle. So the target must be twice as far as the point on the mirror.
A:adimlar.2.metin: You joined two mirrors with 60° between them, and a flag stands in between. The images also give images of each other.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.soru: How many images do you see in the mirrors?
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: If the two mirrors gave only one image each, there would be 2 images. But the images are reflected again in the other mirror.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: Since 360/α = 6 is an even number, the number of images is n = 360/α − 1 = 5. If the angle between the mirrors were 90°, there would be 3 images.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: There are 360/60 = 6 flag positions, but one of them is the object itself. So the number of images is one less.
A:adimlar.3.metin: An object stands in front of a concave mirror with a focal length of 10 cm. The orange ray comes parallel to the principal axis and passes through the focus (F). The green ray reflects symmetrically at the vertex. Slide the object so that the image is real, inverted, and 2 times larger.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.tamam: The object is between F and C (15 cm). The reflected rays crossed beyond C, and the image was real, inverted, and 2 times larger. You will see how to find this by calculation in Card 11.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.ipucu: The object must be outside F but closer than C. When the object is between F and C, the image is real, inverted, and enlarged.
A:adimlar.4.metin: According to Snell's law, n₁·sinθ₁ = n₂·sinθ₂, and in air n = 1. Light arrives from air at 53° (sin 53° ≈ 0.8). Adjust the refractive index of the medium so that the angle of refraction is 30°.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.tamam: Since 1 · 0.8 = n · 0.5, n = 1.6. Light travels in this medium at c/1.6 ≈ 1.9·10⁸ m/s. The larger the index, the more the light bends.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.ipucu: sin 30° = 0.5. Find n from the equation 1 · 0.8 = n · 0.5.
A:adimlar.5.metin: A laser sends light to the boundary between two media. Part of the light reflects, and part passes through by refracting. Change the angle of incidence and the refractive index of the lower medium. You can also send the light the other way. Find out the following for yourself.
A:adimlar.5.kontroller.2.etiket: Send light from the lower medium into air
A:adimlar.5.gorev.bulgular.0.yazi: As light passes from air into glass (n = 1.5), raise the angle of incidence above 80°. Does the light ever fail to get through?
A:adimlar.5.gorev.bulgular.0.tamam: No, the angle of refraction reached about 42° at most. This is the critical angle of glass. Light passing from a smaller index to a larger index always bends toward the normal. There is no total internal reflection in this direction.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.bulgular.1.yazi: Now send the light from glass into air and find an angle at which no light gets out.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.bulgular.1.tamam: When the angle of incidence passed the critical angle (about 42° in glass), all the light reflected back. This is called total internal reflection. This is how a fiber-optic cable traps light.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.bulgular.2.yazi: Make the lower medium diamond (n ≈ 2.42). Find the smallest whole-number angle at which total internal reflection begins.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.bulgular.2.tamam: The critical angle is about 24° in diamond and about 42° in glass. Light entering a diamond is totally reflected many times at the faces and can get out in only a few directions. That is why a diamond sparkles so much.
A:adimlar.6.metin: A yellow ball reflects the red and green of white light and absorbs the blue. Now only a red light will be on in the room.
A:adimlar.6.gorev.soru: How does the yellow ball look in red light?
A:adimlar.6.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: For the ball to look yellow, green light must reach the eye along with red. But there is no green light in the room.
A:adimlar.6.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: The ball reflects red too. It would look black only if there were no light left for it to reflect.
A:adimlar.6.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: The ball reflects the red light that falls on it. Since no green light arrives, the ball looks only red.
A:adimlar.7.metin: The eye works like a converging lens. In a nearsighted eye, rays from far away meet in front of the retina, and distant objects look blurred. Try the two eyeglass lenses one at a time.
A:adimlar.7.gorev.soru: Which eyeglass lens does a nearsighted eye need?
A:adimlar.7.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: A thick-edged lens spreads the rays a little, and the focus shifts back onto the retina.
A:adimlar.7.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: A thin-edged lens converges the rays even more. So the focus moves even farther from the retina.
A:adimlar.7.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: A thin-edged lens converges the rays more, and the focus shifts even farther forward of the retina.
A:kapanis.0: Light travels along straight lines. A point source makes an umbra, and an extended source makes a penumbra as well.
A:kapanis.1: In reflection, the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection. The angles are measured from the normal.
A:kapanis.2: Two angled mirrors (if 360/α is even) form n = 360/α − 1 images.
A:kapanis.3: For mirrors and lenses, 1/f = 1/d<sub>o</sub> + 1/d<sub>i</sub>. The magnification is found with m = −d<sub>i</sub>/d<sub>o</sub>.
A:kapanis.4: According to Snell's law, n₁·sinθ₁ = n₂·sinθ₂. When light passes from a denser medium to a less dense one, there is total internal reflection if the critical angle is exceeded.
A:kapanis.5: An object appears in the color of the light it reflects. A nearsighted eye gets a thick-edged lens, and a farsighted eye a thin-edged lens.
